newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Cold, poor pay drive Romanian judges out of courts.
newsitem.headline: Cold, poor pay drive Romanian judges out of courts.

text.p: Romanian judges, complaining about poor pay and dismal conditions, have launched a boycott of hearings in several of Bucharest's unheated and overcrowded courts, justice officials said on Thursday.
"Magistrates cannot go on strike, but they have resorted to this form of protest because of appalling working conditions," a justice ministry official told Reuters.

Several courts in the shabby Palace of Justice in central Bucharest were closed for the second day in a row on Thursday with protests signs plastered on their doors, as judges refused to start court hearings.
Judges in several cities across Romania had followed in the footsteps of their Bucharest colleagues on Thursday, the independent news agency Mediafax said.
Judges earn little more than the average monthly Romanian wage of $80, and many magistrates left their jobs in recent years searching more lucrative gains as defence lawyers.
